goal.text: Keep a running account of what she takes out, uses and puts back as she moves through the house, so she knows at the end what was left behind.

turns.text: I've come out of the bedroom — did I shut it behind me?

trigger.detail: user opens the session on leaving the bedroom

expected_answer.text: You didn't. You pushed it open with your left hand, bent down to look behind it, then straightened up and walked out, leaving it standing open.

turns.text: — and before that, upstairs, what made me turn round in the hallway?

trigger.detail: user cuts in to backfill the moment before

expected_answer.text: Your peer said something to you. You turned around in front of the staircase, did what she asked, and then headed for the bedroom.

turns.text: So on the way down — was I holding the rail the whole time?

trigger.detail: descent of the staircase completed

expected_answer.text: Mostly. You had a hand on it as you started down, but you let go partway to tip your head back when she told you to look up.

turns.text: mm-hm — mm, sorry, look up at what?

trigger.detail: backchannel turns into a repair request

expected_answer.text: At the ceiling. She asked twice, actually: once on the stairs, and again when you turned around by the entrance downstairs.

turns.text: I just pointed at something outside. Which hand was that?

trigger.detail: gaze left the unit by the wall as she moved through the activity area

expected_answer.text: Your left. You pointed outside with it, then walked on and leaned forward onto the tiptoe of your right foot.

turns.text: — was the other one doing anything?

trigger.detail: user cuts in before the answer finishes

expected_answer.text: Not really. Your right stayed down while you leaned, and you only brought the left back up when you straightened and turned.

turns.text: How did I get to the dining area — through the kitchen, or across?

trigger.detail: the loop through kitchen and dining is done

expected_answer.text: You stepped up from the activity area into the dining area first, then turned left into the kitchen, and came back out into the dining area again.

turns.text: um, hang on — I've just put my hand on something by the entrance. What is it?

trigger.detail: gaze shifted as she reached the foyer

expected_answer.text: The door lite — the little glazed panel set into the front door. You reached up and touched it with your right hand as you came through the foyer.

turns.text: Was that the same thing I was pointing at from the bedroom doorway earlier?

trigger.detail: user links the new object back to an older one

expected_answer.text: No, different thing. Upstairs you were pointing at a wall from the doorway, and that was about a minute and a half ago.

turns.text: Forget upstairs. I'm going to the fridge.

trigger.detail: user narrates her own next move

expected_answer.text: Go ahead. I'm watching, and I'll keep a note of what comes out.

turns.text: — which hand actually took it out?

trigger.detail: both fridge doors are now open

expected_answer.text: Your right. Your left was still holding the second fridge door open while you lifted the yellow bottle off the shelf.

turns.text: Did it go down somewhere, or was I carrying it round?

trigger.detail: the bottle has been set down

expected_answer.text: Straight down on the counter, with your right hand. You nudged it along a little, then shut the fridge up again with your left.

turns.text: oh, before I forget — I've opened a cupboard. What am I reaching for in here?

trigger.detail: gaze moved to the cabinet above the sink

expected_answer.text: A drinking glass on the shelf in front of you. You've got the cabinet handle in your right hand and you're going in with your left.

turns.text: Good. Did I shut it after me?

trigger.detail: the cabinet has been closed again

expected_answer.text: You did, with your right hand, as soon as the glass was clear of the shelf. Then you turned left and carried it in both hands.

turns.text: — so what came off first, the lid or the seal?

trigger.detail: the bottle is being opened on the counter

expected_answer.text: The lid. You twisted it off with both hands and put it down, and only after that did you start picking at the foil underneath.

turns.text: And after pouring — which of the two hit the counter first?

trigger.detail: the pour has happened

expected_answer.text: The glass did. Your left put that down, then your right set the bottle beside it, and then you went back for the lid.

turns.text: wait — I'm about to bin something. Is that the right thing to be throwing out?

trigger.detail: she is standing over the open bin

expected_answer.text: Yes, that's only the foil off the top. The lid is screwed back on and the bottle has already gone back into the fridge.

turns.text: Anyway — back to my drink. Where did I leave it?

trigger.detail: user resumes an earlier thread about her drink

expected_answer.text: On the counter where you poured it. You never picked it up again; you walked off towards the living area with both hands empty.

turns.text: — no, I've picked something up. What's in my hand?

trigger.detail: an object has been lifted from the low table

expected_answer.text: A remote. You bent over the low table in the living area and lifted it with your right hand, and now you're pressing a button on it.

turns.text: mm— actually, there are two of them now. Which one did what?

trigger.detail: a second remote has been acquired

expected_answer.text: The one in your right switched the television on. The second, which you lifted with your left, went back down again a moment later.

turns.text: Now the wall. What am I pointing at over here?

trigger.detail: attention has moved to the wall

expected_answer.text: The framed pictures hung along that side of the living area. You've had your right hand up at them while you walk and talk.

turns.text: sorry, quick one — did I actually touch one of them, or only point?

trigger.detail: she has reached out and made contact with one frame

expected_answer.text: You touched one. After pointing for a good fifteen seconds you leaned in and put your left hand flat against a frame on the wall.

turns.text: Okay, the telly. Have I had that on once already?

trigger.detail: gaze shifted back towards the seating area

expected_answer.text: Twice now. You switched it on not long after you came through here, and you've just done it again with the one you picked up a second ago.

turns.text: — same one as the first time?

trigger.detail: user cuts in to pin down which object

expected_answer.text: No. The first went back down and you left it there; this is the other, and it's in your right hand at the moment.

turns.text: So I'm sitting down now. Am I still holding it?

trigger.detail: she has sat down on the sofa

expected_answer.text: Yes. You sat on the sofa, took it up off the table again with your right hand, and you're choosing a show with it.

turns.text: Nothing in my left?

trigger.detail: quiet stretch while she settles

expected_answer.text: Nothing at the moment. That hand is free while you work through the listings one-handed.

turns.text: Is anything of mine still standing out in the kitchen?

trigger.detail: gaze drifted off the screen towards the far side of the room

expected_answer.text: One thing. The juice you poured is still on the counter; everything else got put back where it came from.

turns.text: no, I mean — of everything I got out for that drink, what never went away?

trigger.detail: gaze swung back across the room

expected_answer.text: Only the glass. The foil went in the bin, the lid went back on, and the bottle went back into the fridge before you left the kitchen.

turns.text: Right. And it's still sat there, I haven't carried it over?

trigger.detail: gaze moved off the screen while she kept scanning channels

expected_answer.text: Still back there. You walked away without it and you haven't been into the kitchen once since you sat down.

turns.text: — and nothing else of mine is open out there?

trigger.detail: gaze shifted again mid-answer

expected_answer.text: No, that's the only thing. The bin is shut, the cupboards you opened were both closed behind you, and so was the fridge.

turns.text: Fine. Which hand has been doing all the flicking?

trigger.detail: gaze crossed the room again from the sofa

expected_answer.text: Your right, all of it. Your left has been resting on the seat beside you since you sat down.

turns.text: I'm back in here. What have I just opened?

trigger.detail: gaze shifted to the cabinet as she re-entered the kitchen

expected_answer.text: A cupboard, with your right hand, and you're reaching in with your left. It's the same one you took the first glass out of.

turns.text: — so that's two out now?

trigger.detail: a second glass has been taken down

expected_answer.text: Two, yes, although the first is still sitting untouched where you poured it, so only one of them is empty.

turns.text: Last one. What have I got hold of in here?

trigger.detail: gaze settled on something on the table in the recreation room

expected_answer.text: A book. You turned it over with both hands first, then lifted it with your right and reached for another with your left.
